title: What happened yesterday
can: Tell a story about yesterday or last year with the pretérito indefinido: fui, comí, vi.
doneText: You can now say what you did yesterday, last weekend or last year, and when Spain uses he comido instead.

skills.pret-er: Past endings for -er and -ir: comí, salió
skills.fui: Fui, fue: ser and ir in the past
skills.pret-odd: The odd ones: hice, estuve, tuve
skills.pret-or-perf: Ayer comí or hoy he comido

discover.intro: Both colours talk about the past. Look at the time words, then at the verbs.

groups.label: A finished time
lines: I spoke to my mum last night.
El sábado fuimos a la playa.
We went to the beach on Saturday.

groups.label: Today or this week
lines: Esta mañana he hablado con mi madre.
I spoke to my mum this morning.
Esta semana hemos ido a la playa.
We've been to the beach this week.

discover.question: What decides which past Spain uses?
options: The time: a finished time like ayer takes one word (comí); today or this week takes he comido.
Whether the sentence is a question.
Whether the verb ends in -ar or -er.
discover.nudge: Not quite. Look at the first word of each sentence: ayer, anoche, el sábado, then hoy, esta mañana, esta semana.
discover.reveal: This is the pretérito indefinido, for things that happened in a time that is over: yesterday, last night, last year. It is one word, with its own endings:

hooks.title: One word, its own endings
rows: I went out with friends last night.
Mi hermana salió tarde y volvió a las dos.
My sister went out late and came back at two.
I went to Toledo on Saturday.

hooks.title: When Spain uses it
rows: I watched a film last night.
La semana pasada fui a Sevilla.
I went to Seville last week.
El año pasado viví en Londres.
I lived in London last year.
Hace dos años estuve en Madrid.
I was in Madrid two years ago.

learn.title: What you did
learn.sub: Tap any row to hear it

blocks.text: -er and -ir verbs share one set of endings: comí, viví, salí. Ser and ir share theirs too: fui means I went or I was, and the rest of the sentence tells you which.
The accent matters. Hablo is I speak, now. Habló is he or she spoke, yesterday. Say the last syllable louder: ha-BLÓ.
Spain splits the past by the time: hoy he comido (today, see chapter 10) but ayer comí (yesterday). If the time is over, use the one-word past. Much of Latin America uses comí for both.

blocks.title: Hoy or ayer
blocks.note: Same event, different time word. Hoy takes he visto, ayer takes vi.

blocks.text: Nosotros of -ar and -ir verbs is the same as now: hablamos, vivimos. The time word tells you it's the past: ayer hablamos.

enAlts: What did you get up to yesterday?

phrases.en: I went to the cinema yesterday.
enAlts: Yesterday I went to the cinema.
I went to the movies yesterday.

phrases.en: I went out with some friends last night.
enAlts: Last night I went out with some friends.
I went out with friends last night.

phrases.en: I was in Barcelona last year.
enAlts: Last year I was in Barcelona.
I went to Barcelona last year.
I had too much to eat.

exercises.why: Yo, in a finished time: hablé. Hablo is now, and habló is he or she.
Comer, yo, in the past: comí, with an accent.

items.why: He trabajado goes with a time that isn't over: hoy.
Trabajé goes with a finished time: ayer.

items.blank: ___ comimos en casa de mi abuela.
items.full: Ayer comimos en casa de mi abuela.
items.why: Comimos is the one-word past: ayer.
Vi is the one-word past: ayer.
Fuimos is the one-word past: ayer.
Salí is the one-word past: ayer.

exercises.say: El verano pasado estuve en Valencia.
options: I was in Valencia last summer.
I'm going to Valencia next summer.
exercises.why: Estuve: I was (somewhere). El verano pasado: last summer.

exercises.q: El sábado ___ a la playa con mis amigos.
exercises.why: Ir in the past, yo: fui. Ser has the same form.

exercises.prompt: Tap the word that is wrong.
exercises.sentence: Ayer mi hermano hablé con el profesor.
exercises.fixed: Ayer mi hermano habló con el profesor.
exercises.why: Mi hermano is él: habló. Hablé is yo.

exercises.prompt: We lived in Seville two years ago.
exercises.answer: Hace dos años vivimos en Sevilla.
exercises.why: Hace dos años means two years ago. It can go first or last.

exercises.q: I went to the cinema yesterday.
exercises.why: Ayer is a finished time, so the one-word past: fui.
Hacer is an odd one: hice, hiciste, hizo.

exercises.prompt: Tap the word that is wrong.
exercises.sentence: Anoche mis padres salió a cenar.
exercises.fixed: Anoche mis padres salieron a cenar.

exercises.why: Llamar, tú: llamaste. Usted: llamó. Vosotros: llamasteis.

exercises.prompt: In Spain, which one is right?
exercises.why: Ayer is over, so Spain uses comí. He comido is for today or this week.
Ser in the past, for something that's over: fue. Spain also says estuvo genial.

write.title: Say it in your own words
write.task: Write a short message to a friend about last weekend: where you went, what you did and how it was.
write.starter: El sábado fui…  Por la noche…  Fue…
write.model: El sábado fui a Toledo con mi hermana. Vimos la catedral y comimos en un restaurante pequeño. Por la noche volvimos a Madrid en tren. Fue un día genial.
checklist: The one-word past for a finished time: fui, vimos, comimos
A time word: el sábado, ayer, anoche

boss.title: Monday at the office
boss.persona: You are Lucía, a friendly colleague at an office in Valencia. It is Monday morning. Ask the learner what they did at the weekend, where they went, who with, and how it was. Use tú, as colleagues do in Spain. Speak European Spanish, using the pretérito indefinido for the weekend.

turns.npc: ¡Hola! ¿Qué tal el fin de semana? ¿Qué hiciste?
turns.en: Hi! How was the weekend? What did you do?
choices: Fui a la playa con unos amigos.
Voy a la playa con unos amigos.
Voy is now. The weekend is over: fui.
Fue a la playa con unos amigos.
Fue is he, she or usted. About yourself: fui.

turns.en: Great! And which beach did you go to?
choices: Fuimos a la Malvarrosa.
Fueron a la Malvarrosa.
Fueron is they. You and your friends are nosotros: fuimos.
Fuimos en la Malvarrosa.
Going to a place takes a: fuimos a la Malvarrosa.
Sí, comimos una paella al lado del mar.
Sí, comemos una paella al lado del mar.
Comemos is now. In the past: comimos.
Sí, comieron una paella al lado del mar.
Comieron is they. You and your friends: comimos.
Fue genial, pero llegué a casa muy tarde.
Fui genial, pero llegué a casa muy tarde.
Fui is I was. The day was great: fue.
Es genial, pero llegué a casa muy tarde.
Es is now. The weekend is over: fue.

boss.closing: ¡Qué envidia! Yo me quedé en casa todo el fin de semana.
boss.closingEn: I'm so jealous! I stayed at home all weekend.
boss.chatOpeningEn: And what did you do on Sunday?
